title: What is Three.js?
description: Three.js is a powerful JavaScript library that brings 3D graphics to the web. Built on WebGL, it abstracts away the complexity and gives developers a clean, intuitive API for creating stunning 3D scenes, animations, and interactive experiences.
code:
<group ref={ref}>
  <mesh position={[-2, 0, 0]}>
    <boxGeometry args={[1, 1, 1]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.blue} metalness={0.7} roughness={0.3} />
  </mesh>
  <mesh position={[0, 0, 0]}>
    <sphereGeometry args={[0.7, 32, 32]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.green} metalness={0.7} roughness={0.3} />
  </mesh>
  <mesh position={[2, 0, 0]}>
    <torusGeometry args={[0.5, 0.2, 16, 100]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.purple} metalness={0.7} roughness={0.3} />
  </mesh>
</group>

title: Understanding 3D
description: Three-dimensional graphics create depth and immersion. We'll start from the basics: Vertices, Edges, and Faces.

title: Vertices: The Foundation
description: Vertices are the fundamental points that define 3D geometry. Each vertex has X, Y, and Z coordinates in 3D space.

title: Edges: Connecting the Dots
description: Edges connect vertices together, creating the wireframe skeleton of your 3D object.

title: Faces: Adding Surfaces
description: Faces are the surfaces created when three or more vertices connect. With faces, we can apply materials, colors, and textures.
code:
<mesh geometry={canGeometry}>
  <meshStandardMaterial
    color={COLORS.teal}
    metalness={0.8}
    roughness={0.2}
  />
  <Edges geometry={edgesGeometry} color="#000000" threshold={0} />
</mesh>

title: React Three Fiber Basics
description: R3F makes Three.js feel like React. Props map directly to Three.js properties.
code:
<mesh ref={ref} position={[1, 0, 0]} rotation={[0, Math.PI / 4, 0]}>
  <boxGeometry args={[2, 2, 2]} />
  <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.hotpink} />
</mesh>

title: Geometry and Shapes
description: Geometries define the shape of 3D objects. Use the `args` prop to pass constructor arguments.
code:
<group ref={ref}>
  <mesh position={[-2.5, 0, 0]}>
    <boxGeometry args={[1, 1.5, 0.5]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.blue} />
  </mesh>
  <mesh position={[-0.8, 0, 0]}>
    <sphereGeometry args={[0.7, 32, 32]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.green} />
  </mesh>
  <mesh position={[0.8, 0, 0]}>
    <torusGeometry args={[0.5, 0.15, 16, 100]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.purple} />
  </mesh>
  <mesh position={[2.5, 0, 0]}>
    <cylinderGeometry args={[0.5, 0.5, 1, 32]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial color={COLORS.orange} />
  </mesh>
</group>

title: Materials & Textures
description: Materials define how surfaces look, while textures add detail and realism.

title: Your First Scene
description: Putting it all together: your first R3F scene.
code:
<> 
  <mesh ref={ref}>
    <boxGeometry args={[2, 2, 2]} />
    <meshStandardMaterial />
  </mesh>
  <ambientLight intensity={0.1} />
  <directionalLight position={[0, 0, 5]} color="red" intensity={0.8} />
</>

title: Interactive Showcase
description: Combine vertices, edges, and faces to create interactive 3D experiences.
